subject: a97A02:B4 — why the primitive route instead of the symmetric-difference estimate

nodes.claim: Why not prove continuity by estimating the symmetric difference of the two windows, as the informal solution does?

The symmetric-difference estimate needs the restriction |s-t| ≤ 2h (the difference has measure 2 min(|s-t|, 2h), not 2|s-t|), exponent bookkeeping in 1/q, and a separate p = 1 fallback through absolute continuity of the integral; writing the moving integral as a difference of two continuous primitives handles every p ≥ 1 at once.

The symmetric-difference measure is 2 min(|s-t|, 2h) — the informal solution's 2|s-t| fails once the windows are disjoint — and the L^q estimate degenerates at q = ∞, where p = 1 needs absolute continuity instead.
Bound |f_h(t) - f_h(s)| by ‖f‖_p times the L^q norm of g_{t,h} - g_{s,h}, supported on the symmetric difference.
Write the moving window integral as F(t+h) - F(t-h) for the fixed primitive F of the integrable function f.
The restricted Lebesgue measure is atomless, which is what makes the half-line primitive continuous.
The Icc window integral equals the difference of the two Iic primitives, by the interval-integral identity.
Continuity of a difference of compositions of a continuous primitive with continuous translations.
t ↦ ∫_{[t-h,t+h]} f is continuous on [0,1] for every p ≥ 1, with no case distinction.
Dividing by the constant 2h, f_h is continuous on [0,1] for all 1 ≤ p < ∞ at once.
